source_claim_verbatim_translation: The relationship between the cup product and Steenrod operations.
canonical_statement: Provisional intended scope: Steenrod operations obey a product formula for the cup product. The repository wording does not yet determine whether the root is the mod-2 component formula Sq^n(x cup y) = sum_{i+j=n} Sq^i(x) cup Sq^j(y), its total-square form, or an odd-prime reduced-power analogue.
domain_and_universes: Open: a selected category of spaces (or equivalent cochain model), coefficient field, cohomological degrees, and a graded cohomology ring; Lean universes and concrete encodings remain unfrozen.
quantifiers: space or cochain object X in the selected theory
cohomology classes x and y of specified degrees
operation degree n (and prime p if an odd-prime version is selected)
hypotheses: cup product and Steenrod operations are defined in the same cohomology theory
coefficient and grading hypotheses required by the selected operation family
all indexing and instability conventions fixed by the statement phase
conclusion: A componentwise or total-operation multiplicativity identity relating a Steenrod operation on x cup y to products of operations on x and y.
statement_choices_requiring_source_audit: mod-2 Steenrod squares versus odd-prime reduced powers and Bockstein variants
component formula versus total-operation ring-homomorphism formulation
ordinary singular cohomology of spaces versus another cochain/cohomology model
grading, index ranges, Koszul signs, and out-of-range conventions
naturality and instability laws as context or separate theorems

alternate_encodings.target: Sq(x cup y) = Sq(x) cup Sq(y) for the total Steenrod square
alternate_encodings.relationship: candidate equivalent to all mod-2 component identities after finite graded expansion

alternate_encodings.target: P^n(x cup y) = sum_{i+j=n} P^i(x) cup P^j(y) at an odd prime
alternate_encodings.relationship: analogue, not automatically identical to the mod-2 root

excluded_degenerate_cases: No boundary case is excluded yet. Degree-zero operations, the cohomological unit, zero classes, out-of-range indices, empty/trivial spaces, and odd-prime sign conventions must be explicit statement mutations or boundary probes.
